newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains against the dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains against the dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Thursday in dull trading, dealers said.
"During the last two days the local market has been very quiet as investors await the release of the November CPI and approval of the 1997 budget," said Gideon Sadeh of Bank Leumi.
The November consumer price index is due to be released on Sunday.
"The session opened with a mild rise of the shekel after the decline of the dollar abroad on Wednesday. During the day trading was mixed and dull," Sadeh added.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2820 shekels against 3.2860 shekels on Wednesday. The basket composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6681 shekels against 3.6750 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8988 shekels per 100 yen versus 2.9139 on Wednesday and against the mark at 2.1242 shekels versus 2.1299 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar continued to trade at 3.2820 shekels.
